clue.text: Brag aloud, quiet about one's element

indicators.note: aloud says a word is to be taken as it sounds when spoken, not as spelt

parts.note: to brag is to crow

indicators.note: about says one piece goes around another, here the word for quiet wrapping the one

parts.note: mum means quiet, as in 'keep mum'
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is 'is', joining it on

explanation.surface: Someone who boasts loudly is told to pipe down about their own element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aloud' works on the boast word only; 'about' has the quiet word wrapping the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallic chemical element used in plating, symbol Cr.

clue.text: Beast's antler cut and twisted at the end, almost gaping

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: twisted at the end says only the last two letters swap round
cut says a letter is snipped off the word antler

parts.note: taken as written before it is trimmed

indicators.note: almost says the last letter of the word for gaping is dropped

parts.note: gaping means open

explanation.surface: A wild animal's damaged, bent antler leaves it looking open-mouthed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the antler; 'twisted at the end' swaps the final pair of what is left, and 'almost' trims the last letter of OPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A swift horned grazing animal of Africa and Asia is a beast.

clue.text: Where to find knickers here, one could say

definitions.text: Where to find knickers here, one could say

parts.words: Where to find knickers here, one could say
parts.note: said aloud, 'knickers here' sounds like the island's capital city Nicosia, so the clue asks where that city is

explanation.surface: Someone asks where in the room their underwear can be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one could say' signals a sound: 'knickers here' is said like Nicosia, the capital of this Mediterranean island.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of this eastern Mediterranean island nation.

clue.text: Irregular pulse stopped by snoring, of which this is an example

definitions.text: of which this is an example
definitions.note: plural: this crossword is one example of the kind of thing meant

indicators.note: stopped by says the snoring sound plugs the gap inside the jumbled letters
an irregular pulse is uneven, so the letters of pulse are jumbled

parts.note: ZZ is the comic-strip sign for someone snoring

explanation.surface: A sleeper's snoring interrupts an erratic heartbeat, and the setter winks at the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stopped by' puts the snore inside the jumbled pulse; the definition points back at the crossword itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A crossword is a kind of brain-teaser, so this grid is itself one example.

clue.text: Where to study cattle crossing?

parts.note: an ox is one of the cattle
a bridge is a crossing over a river or road

explanation.surface: Someone asks where you go to learn about herds fording a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: OXBRIDGE is the British blend of Oxford and Cambridge, the two oldest English universities.
explanation.definitionFit: The combined name for Oxford and Cambridge universities, places of higher learning.

clue.text: Many people from Croatia in this movie

parts.note: a large number
Dalmatia is the coastal region of Croatia, so its natives are Dalmatians

explanation.surface: A film with a huge Croatian cast.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as Croats; the solver must spot the spotted dogs of the Disney film, named after the Croatian coastal region.
explanation.definitionFit: A Disney animated film about a pack of spotted dogs pursued by Cruella de Vil.

clue.text: False U-turn maybe supported by Spain

indicators.note: in a down answer, supported by puts the second piece underneath the first
maybe says the letters might be arranged some other way

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A claimed reversal of policy turns out to be false, at least with Spanish backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' is the anagram signal, and 'supported by' stacks Spain's letter beneath in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untrue is false, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: We are obliged to break out to capture accessory

indicators.note: to capture says the rearranged letters hold the accessory inside
break says the letters of out are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: a hanky, or handkerchief, is a pocket accessory

explanation.surface: Someone is forced to escape in order to grab a fashion item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' looks like a link but belongs to the container signal 'to capture'; 'break' scrambles the word out.
explanation.definitionFit: An expression of gratitude, said when one feels obliged to someone.

clue.text: Love being turned over after kiss — it's a gas!

indicators.note: after puts the reversed word behind the kiss

parts.note: X is the kiss at the end of a letter

indicators.note: turned over says the word for love is read backwards

parts.note: love in tennis is a score of nothing, or none

explanation.surface: A kiss followed by a romantic upset is a laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is tennis's zero; 'being turned over' reads it backwards, and 'after' puts it behind the kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A noble gas used in bright lamps, element number 54.

clue.text: See 2
Cutter's instrument is very cutting

parts.note: a razor is a cutter, and the 's makes it razor's
a harp is a stringed musical instrument

explanation.surface: A barber's tool is pointed out to be extremely sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the start as RAZOR'S HARP, a musical instrument belonging to a cutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen-edged, and figuratively a biting or incisive remark is very cutting.

clue.text: Animals in some hardship, possibly

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Creatures suffering some hardship, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Large African river mammals are animals, a plain category definition.

clue.text: Fox trapped by mother owls?

definitions.note: the collective noun for a group of owls; the question mark flags the odd usage

indicators.note: trapped by says the name sits inside the word for mother

parts.note: a mother is a parent
Liam Fox is a British Conservative politician, so Fox gives his first name

explanation.surface: A fox is caught by a mother owl, or several.
explanation.walkthrough: Liam Fox is a UK MP, nicely placed inside the House's own name; a group of owls is called a parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: Collective noun: a flock of owls is traditionally termed this, as a gaggle is for geese.

clue.text: Extreme indignation risk

parts.note: the extreme of something is its end
indignation is anger

explanation.surface: Extreme outrage is a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something at risk is to imperil it; both are verbs here.

clue.text: Central assembly couple have a hug

indicators.note: central picks the middle two letters of assembly

parts.note: a brace is a couple, as in a brace of pheasants

explanation.surface: A pair at a central meeting hall share a cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To hug or clasp someone in your arms; both are verb phrases.

clue.text: Nice gesture to go out with? In a way, yes

parts.note: to court someone is to woo or date them

indicators.note: in a way says the letters of yes are taken some other way, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is asked out and answers, sort of, yes, a pleasant gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a way' rearranges YES into ESY.
explanation.definitionFit: A polite act of good manners is a pleasing gesture.

clue.text: Do-it-yourself sea trip is a long and lonely time

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble, so the letters fall over into a new order

explanation.surface: A solo self-organised voyage is a long, lonely spell.
explanation.walkthrough: With 6 down's number, this gives the novel by Gabriel García Márquez, One Hundred Years of Solitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Years spent alone describes an extended period of isolation.

clue.text: Drunk Romeo slurping up French wine is not a discriminating consumer

indicators.note: slurping says the jumbled letters take the wine in
drunk says the letters of Romeo stagger into a new order
up in a down answer says the wine word is read bottom to top

parts.note: vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A tipsy Romeo gulping French wine is hardly a connoisseur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' scrambles Romeo, 'slurping' takes the wine inside, and 'up' reads the French word bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal that eats both plants and meat is an indiscriminate eater.

clue.text: Over and above part section of house

indicators.note: part says the answer is a piece taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something extra, part of a house.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed open gallery along the outside of a building forms part of it.

clue.text: See 17
Nothing clear about this prediction

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing

indicators.note: about says the letters of clear are turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: Nothing is clear regarding this forecast.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophecy given by a seer, as at Delphi, is a prediction.

clue.text: See 6
Pretend to be like birds heading north

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: in a down answer, heading north says the bird word reads upwards

parts.note: emus are large flightless birds

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be birds migrating north.
explanation.definitionFit: To assume a manner is to put it on, to feign it.

clue.text: See 6
Heartbroken part in screen role voluntarily rejected

indicators.note: rejected says the run is thrown back, read right to left
part in says a run of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: An actor turns down a film part of their own accord and is crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part in' takes NROLEVOL from 'screen role voluntarily', and 'rejected' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Forlorn and pining after losing a sweetheart, so in grief over romance.

clue.text: See 24 across
Cat in conversation chain

indicators.note: in conversation says the word is taken as it is spoken

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat

explanation.surface: A cat appears in a series of chats.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain is made of connected rings joined one to the next.

clue.text: Sweet thing in extremely delicate meringue skirt

indicators.note: extremely takes the outer letters of delicate and meringue

parts.note: a ra-ra skirt is a short frilly skirt of the 1980s

explanation.surface: A sweet treat is set in a very fine meringue skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A ra-ra skirt is a short tiered skirt, popular in 1980s Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown cane sugar, so something sweet, a crossword-style definition.
